scope: Independent review of the finite PDSerialHID scheduler and frozen client marker contract. No source edits, device access, hardware execution or physical-input claim.

checks.additional_checks: In-memory imports and synthetic feed/tick calls reproduced the findings below; no serial backend was opened.

findings.title: READY can resurrect an expired schedule
findings.reproduction: Prime at t=0 and emit the five packets through t=0.8. Without another tick, feed exact READY at t=31. The old deadline 30 becomes 41; tick(31) emits A-down with no error.
findings.impact: Deadline enforcement depends on callback ordering. The newly observed ConsoleSession.advance_virtual calls feed before tick, so this is not prevented by that integration.
findings.fix: Check the existing deadline before accepting any incoming barrier that can extend or advance the schedule. Expiration must be sticky and clear pending actions.
findings.test: Feed READY at and after the original deadline before tick; assert sticky failure, unchanged emitted-action count and no A-down. Repeat with a fragmented READY whose terminating newline arrives after expiry.

findings.title: Contradictory pointer-motion evidence does not cancel a queued click
findings.reproduction: After key completion, feed exact POINTER_ENTER x=200.0000 y=100.0000 followed in the same chunk by POINTER_MOTION x=500.0000 y=100.0000. tick emits the button-down packet and error stays null.
findings.limit: This is a synthetic defensive-parser case. The frozen client rejects this out-of-point motion before printing its motion marker and subsequently emits its error. It is not observed hardware output or an expected valid frozen-client trace.
findings.fix: Validate recognized pointer-motion evidence during the content-point/click phases and cancel pending buttons immediately on wrong or malformed coordinates. Keep subsequent titlebar drag motion outside this pre-click coordinate rule.
findings.test: ENTER plus contradictory MOTION in one feed must produce no button; valid same-point MOTION must retain the normal sequence.

findings.title: Malformed coordinate escapes the sticky failure path
findings.reproduction: At await_point, POINTER_ENTER x=.. y=100.0000 matches the regex, then float('..') raises ValueError; phase remains await_point and error is null.
findings.limit: Not an output generated by the frozen client's finite f64 formatting. The current ConsoleSession outer exception handler stops and records this error, but the standalone helper does not satisfy its own sticky-failure contract.
findings.fix: Use a bounded decimal grammar matching the emitted coordinate syntax and catch conversion failures into fail(); retain the finite/range checks.
findings.test: Malformed, repeated-dot, NaN/Inf and out-of-range coordinates fail without throwing or emitting a click, and later valid markers cannot resume the schedule.

findings.title: A press is accepted before A-down emission
findings.reproduction: Feed READY then exact key=30 state=pressed before the next tick. key_pressed becomes true with zero keying actions emitted.
findings.fix: Require the corresponding A-down action to have been emitted before accepting its press observation, and preserve the existing release-after-up ordering. Integration must additionally bind emitted actions to successful writes and the attempted-TX ledger.
findings.test: A press between READY and the first keying tick fails. A press after the emitted down, followed by emitted up and observed release, still passes.

findings.title: Pointer endpoint conversion exceeds the advertised absolute range
findings.reproduction: pointer(2559,1599,0) emits coordinates 32773 and 32777, while the PDSerialHID axis maximum is 32767.
findings.fix: Clamp the quantized result to 0..32767 or explicitly restrict the public helper to the fixed interior points. The current schedule uses interior coordinates and is unaffected.
findings.test: Both endpoints encode inside the descriptor range.

qualified_source_properties: READY and INPUT_OBSERVED spellings exactly match frozen client main.rs lines 153 and 156, including origin, key/button codes and tolerance.
Priming is full release, left Shift down, full release, followed by two changed button-free absolute reports. No printable key or CRLF framing is introduced.
Keyboard encoder rejects arbitrary usages, boolean integers and modified A. Only release, Shift priming and unmodified usage 4 are allowed.
The content ENTER barrier requires finite coordinates within one pixel of local (200,100), matching the frozen client's explicit tolerance. Initial mismatched ENTER refuses buttons.
Exact nonce-bound INPUT_OBSERVED in await_observed is required before the single fixed six-packet titlebar drag; the final report releases the button.
The normal schedule is 16 packets, with 150 ms minimum pacing, an independent 24-action/1024-byte bound, no retry branch and explicit cancellation.
The helper contains no transport access and makes no physical keyboard or trackpad claim.

integration_observation.status: Source changed concurrently from the initially described unwired state; only a bounded read of ConsoleSession was made, not a full integration approval.
qualified: advance_virtual is called by the existing secondary-CDC reader/writer, including empty-read ticks; no additional serial reader or timer writer is added in this inspected code.
send records attempted bytes and fsyncs before the device write, rejects short writes, and the owner exception path fails the schedule.
Finalization signals finish, joins the owner before cancelling/reporting/closing and refuses an unknown still-running worker.
remaining_contract: tick advances its action count and final phase before the actual transport write. schedule_completed alone is emission bookkeeping, never target acceptance or proof of drag.
Keep final write failures, attempted TX, owner errors, client observation and framebuffer displacement separate. A partial SOH frame must not trigger guessed resynchronization or retries.
Priming must finish before the launcher opens the input consumer, with the agreed node/readiness barrier. The helper cannot establish this script-side contract itself.
No successful hardware send, virtual-input runtime, drag, cleanup or physical input is established by this review.

ordered_next_steps: Root fixes V1 and V4, makes malformed/contradictory pointer observations fail closed, and adds the focused regression cases above.
Rerun the helper and same-owner integration tests, including failed/short final writes and cancellation while waiting between packets; bind the reviewed source hashes.
Keep the real-client observation, finite TX ledger and eventual framebuffer displacement as separate evidence in any later root-authorized test.
